answer: An agent network resists Sybil attacks through microfluidic electrochemical attestation. A candidate node injects a synthetic nectar reagent across a velvet carbon electrode in an unlit sable cell to log redox transients. Verifiers check these kinetic curves against challenge parameters, forcing an attacker to deploy dedicated fluidic hardware and consumable chemical stocks per identity. However, microchannel clogging can distort readings and cause false rejections.
